status: Removed visible-aura application lifetime repaired separately from Corrupted's health threshold. Evidence below retains both native failures and the completed stress comparison; client verification remains pending.
reproduction: Extended real Corrupted release testing exposed a second crash after the earlier charmed-Player loot repair: AuraApplication::ClientUpdate+679 -> Unit::_UpdateSpells. Disassembly places the fault on the application's target pointer after packet construction. Temporary identity-only diagnostics, with no skipping or fake callbacks, confirmed pending raw application addresses absent from the target's live m_appliedAuras map. They occur on24/10-percent self-release and on actual Player/Pet damage release. A16-repeat native run then faults in AuraApplication::ClientUpdate+157 with the diagnostic immediately before it. Both crash logs are retained. The diagnostics are removed from the final implementation.
repair: Unit::_UnapplyAura already removes visible state before effect/linked cleanup. Detach the exact application again after all linked aura-specific cleanup, while the local AuraApplicationPtr still owns it and the target Unit is alive. This prevents a removed application's raw address from surviving into ClientUpdate after Aura releases it. Do not dereference target pointers later from a generic application destructor.

RemoveVisibleAura erases both containers by pointer identity/iterator. The containers compare slot numbers for their ordering, so erase(key) could instead erase a replacement application already using that same slot. Final detachment must preserve that replacement. No slot renumbering, packet suppression, ID whitelist, shared hook bypass or aura-duration change is introduced.
verification: Test-VisibleAuraRemoval compiles the extracted production RemoveVisibleAura and actual slot comparator with std::set and Boost flat_set. It checks ordinary removal, unrelated entries, a different live application in the same slot, and a retired queued pointer. The repaired handler makes zero slot reads during removal. Pinned f5f06838 extraction fails on the same-slot replacement case before reaching the retired-pointer test; the original implementation is not executed on deliberately freed storage.

The native control stress uses the separately pending data-based25-percent Corrupted repair to exercise repeated self-removal. All8 difficulty/faction cases pass; the two Mythic cases each repeat both actual Player and Pet damage release16times, totaling64 releases and128 start/damaged trace markers. Native aura/spell dispatch, charm removal, transform/Bleak cleanup, faction/control restoration and eight-second residual-cast checks execute without errors or a crash. This is a pending-content integration input, not a claim that the Corrupted threshold change is part of this core commit.

AuraScript reentry regression passes. Normal generated CMake Release paths are used. Bounded PE/thunk inspection confirms the final RemoveVisibleAura call follows HandleAuraSpecificMods in actual deployed Unit::_UnapplyAura. Final related regressions and startup are recorded with the next Corrupted audit.
retained_limits: This is a native lifetime/identity repair. It does not establish authenticated client aura icons, input, camera, pet portrait, visuals/audio or full raid survivability.

The first charmed-Player damage crash is a separate preceding fix f5f06838. Corrupted's original11-percent check and post-release cast are separate content defects documented in trial-helya-control-damage-2026-10-20.json and addressed by the subsequent content commit.
